adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the updated fallback logic in `updateEvent` is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the only time the `find(...)` branch runs), the predicate compares each `cal.externalId` to that same falsy value (e.g., `undefined`/`null`), which will almost always fail and return `undefined`. This effectively removes the prior fallback behavior (previously `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) and can cause updates to target no calendar id (or rely on downstream defaults), i.e., a real correctness bug introduced by the diff. The same flawed pattern also appears in `deleteEvent`.

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch), it is typically `undefined`/`null`, so the `.find(...)` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`) and will not match the intended destination calendar. In Office365CalendarService.createEvent, the diff changes destinationCalendar to an array but the implementation still destructures only the first entry (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];`) and builds `eventsUrl` from that single calendar’s externalId. Meanwhile, EventManager now iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, but CalendarManager.createEvent does not pass that `externalId` into the provider createEvent call (it calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`), and Office365CalendarService doesn’t accept/select by externalId/credentialId anyway. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:127-130 — createEvent (and createAttendees/updateEvent/deleteEvent) use only the first destinationCalendar entry, so Lark never creates/updates/deletes the event across all hosts' destination calendars in a collective event (confidence 85, severity P1).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array (`DestinationCalendar[] | null`) and the core flow now iterates destinations in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination. However, `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` still derives `calendarId` via `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ??
